scope.flow: transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 amount) on TokenWrapper
scope.environment: Ethereum ERC-20 TokenWrapper contract and off-chain consumers of Transfer events

entities.name: Block explorers, wallets, indexers, tax tools
Smart contract integrations listening to Transfer events

statements.text: A user or contract calls transferFrom to move tokens on behalf of another address using an allowance.
The from parameter identifies the actual token holder whose balance is debited.
The spender calls transferFrom(from, to, amount) on TokenWrapper.
TokenWrapper emits a Transfer event for the transferFrom operation.
The implementation substitutes msg.sender (the spender) for the from address in the Transfer event emission instead of the token holder whose balance decreases.
Per EIP-20, the Transfer event emitted by transferFrom must set the from parameter to the address of the token holder whose balance decreases.

The emitted Transfer event identifies the transaction initiator (msg.sender, the spender) as the source of the tokens rather than the actual token holder, creating a permanent incorrect record in blockchain history.

Block explorers such as Etherscan and Blockscout parsing the incorrect events display the operator or router contract as the originating address, and users do not see their TokenWrapper transfers in their sent transactions list.

Wallet applications including MetaMask, Rainbow, and Coinbase Wallet populate inaccurate transaction histories and portfolio tracking because transfers are attributed to msg.sender rather than the token holder.

Off-chain indexers such as The Graph subgraphs and Dune Analytics attribute TokenWrapper activity to router contracts and operators rather than actual users, and tax reporting tools fail to detect TokenWrapper transfers, potentially causing incomplete tax reporting and compliance issues.

Smart contract integrations listening to Transfer events, such as DAO treasury tracking, token-gated access controls, referral tracking, and rewards distribution, incorrectly credit activity to operator contracts rather than users, breaking composability.
Off-chain systems and contract integrations rely on Transfer event emissions to attribute token movements to senders.

ambiguities: Report states internal _balanceOf accounting is updated correctly, so no on-chain balance loss is claimed; only event-log misattribution.
No specific actor authorization or permissionless-call claim is made; the spender is described generically as a user or contract using an allowance.
Tax reporting and compliance issues are stated as potential ('potentially causing'), not confirmed.
Severity is classified Medium; no quantified monetary loss is provided.
